instructions: Continue from the exact clean transportable RUN-146-003 candidate fc1383b07265716d23c402bbc656ffe768891e98. Preserve all existing TASK-146 implementation and test updates; do not restart PRIMARY and do not modify tests/test_operator.py because its stale Antigravity assertion is now proven fixed.

RUN-146-003 is semantically very close to completion: verification.py passed 17/17, smoke/self-host passed 41/41, Brain Sync + Brain Ingress passed 21/21, the Antigravity operator focused set passed 4/4, the complete suite passed 1198/1198, and git diff --check passed. The only terminal failure occurred after all verification commands, while deleting the external Windows temp root.

The remaining defect is deterministic cleanup robustness. _remove_temp_root currently retries shutil.rmtree only three times with 0.05s * attempt delays and its onerror handler retries the failed remove immediately after chmod. On Windows a Git object can remain transiently locked longer than this even after tests/processes have exited, producing WinError 5. Strengthen only the cleanup boundary with a bounded Windows-safe retry/backoff policy long enough to absorb short-lived file-handle release latency while remaining deterministic and fail-closed.

Keep the existing permission/read-only recovery: for permission errors clear writable attributes and retry. Add a bounded retry helper for the failed unlink/rmdir operation itself and/or a bounded whole-tree retry with an explicit small maximum elapsed window. Do not ignore errors, use unbounded sleeps, shell out to destructive commands, kill processes, or declare success while temp_root still exists. After the bounded window, residual cleanup must still raise and Runtime must preserve all verification evidence.

Add focused deterministic tests that simulate transient PermissionError/WinError-5-style deletion for more than one immediate attempt and prove eventual cleanup within the bound, plus a persistent permission failure test proving the bounded policy exhausts and fails closed. Keep the existing read-only Git-object cleanup and raw-evidence-retention coverage.

Because src/aios_renew/verification.py is itself Runtime-loaded code, the CODE_FIX continuation may still execute canonical verification with the already-imported RUN-146-003 cleanup implementation in that same process. Do not compensate by changing unrelated code or tests. The Executor only commits the bounded cleanup fix; if that same process later fails solely in old cleanup after all commands pass, preserve the clean candidate so a fresh NO_CHANGE continuation can verify it with the newly loaded implementation.

Do not modify smoke guards, Brain Sync/Ingress tests, Antigravity behavior, TASK-145, TASK-144, or TASK-140. Runtime owns canonical verification; no skips, xfails, filters, verification retries, or safety weakening are permitted.

The isolated Windows temp directory must be created before commands execute, shared by all commands in one verification execution, not mutate the parent process environment, and be cleaned deterministically after verification completes or fails. Failure to create or clean the isolation boundary must fail closed.

task.problem: TASK-145 RUN-145-001 produced a clean transportable candidate 80f54e767b2a86e59f9b4b135430d229ed10059e and passed both focused Unified State commands: 14 passed / 28 deselected and 42 passed. The final Runtime-owned full suite failed with 28 unrelated failures (1173 passed). The dominant deterministic cause is Windows verification TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR isolation under .git/aios/verification/.../temporary. Pytest tmp_path therefore creates test workspaces inside the canonical repository ancestry. Smoke helpers intentionally reject such workspaces, and Git commands from a nominal "non-git" tmp directory discover the enclosing canonical .git, producing false-positive repository detection. Additional failures are stale tests relative to already-canonical behavior: Brain Sync still expects the completed control-plane-closure track although .ai/roadmap-state.yaml now declares active_track brain-portability; Brain Ingress workflow tests still assume one dispatch and pre-REPAIR receipt env although the workflow now has separate safe publication and REPAIR wakeup dispatches; and three Antigravity operator assertions still expect the obsolete prompt/read-only command contract already identified during TASK-144 verification. These failures are outside TASK-145 r1 scope, so repairing RUN-145-001 cannot make its required full suite green.
